summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance. In Alabama the age of majority is 19 (Ala. Code § 26-1-1), and for child abuse and neglect reporting a "child" is a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services (Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3)).
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Ala. Code § 26-14-3 (Title 26, Ch. 14) — Mandatory reporting of child abuse or neglect. Amended by Act 2026-375: the Legislature's code viewer carries one version effective until 10/1/2026 and one effective 10/1/2026. The reporter categories carry over into the 10/1/2026 version as subdivision (a)(2)a.–aa., which also requires the written report within 72 hours of the oral report
Ala. Code § 12-15-308 (Title 12, Ch. 15) — 72-hour shelter care hearing after a child is removed
Ala. Code § 12-15-306 — Removing a child from the custody of a parent, legal guardian, or legal custodian
Ala. Code § 26-14-6 — Temporary protective custody; custody shall not exceed 72 hours
Ala. Code § 38-2-6 — Duties, powers, and responsibilities of the State Department of Human Resources

Ala. Code § 26-14-7.1 — Due process rights for persons under investigation by the department. The hearing package (counsel, witnesses, cross-examination, subpoenas, exculpatory evidence, an impartial hearing officer, and 10 departmental working days to request the hearing in writing) runs only to a person who "is employed by, serves as a volunteer for, holds a license or certificate for, or is connected with any facility, agency, or home which cares for and controls any children" that is licensed, approved, certified, state-operated, or exempt from licensing; a parent investigated in their own home is not in that class
Ala. Code § 38-7-3 (Title 38, Ch. 7 — Child Care) — License to operate a child-care facility; inspections and investigations
Ala. Code § 12-15-315 — Permanency hearing (Department of Human Resources cases)
Ala. Code § 12-15-319 — Grounds for termination of parental rights
Ala. Code § 12-15-117 — Juvenile court jurisdiction continues until the child turns 21

Ala. Code § 26-14-3 as amended by Act 2026-375, § 6 — mandatory reporting text effective 10/1/2026 (oral report to a law enforcement official or the Department of Human Resources, written report within 72 hours, reporter categories relisted as (a)(2)a.–aa.)

Ala. Code § 26-14-1(3) — "CHILD" for child abuse and neglect reporting: a person under 18, or a person under 19 who is in need of protective services and does not qualify for adult protective services under Title 38, Chapter 9
Ala. Code § 26-1-1 — Age of majority designated as 19 years
